notes: No amp+cab block — running into the real tube amp per usual rig rules. Added an EXPERIMENTAL Cali Rectifire (Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier) Preamp-only block since the Dual Rectifier is the specifically confirmed amp the ProCo RAT was driving for Everlong's heavy tone (unlike Nevermind's three-way amp tossup, this is a single well-documented pairing). Two-snapshot design matching the song's core quiet/loud structure: a light-gain, near-clean intro/verse tone that still lets a bit of grit through under hard picking, and a fully driven RAT-into-cranked-amp chorus/bridge tone with layered Drop D guitars. Confirmed rig: ProCo RAT distortion into a cranked Mesa/Boogie Dual/Triple Rectifier for the heavy parts, Boss DM-2 Analog Delay as a long-standing Grohl pedalboard constant. Lace Sensor / Super Champ XD compensation applied via a mild always-on Stupor OD ahead of the RAT and raised Parametric EQ Level.
confirmed_sources: Guitar.com — The Guitar Gear Used on The Foo Fighters' The Colour and the Shape (ProCo RAT/Rat 2, DigiTech Whammy and other pedals sent to Bear Creek Studios; Everlong's driving tone from RAT into a cranked amp, Drop D layered guitars)

Reverb News — The Gear of Foo Fighters (Boss DM-2 Analog Delay, Boss DD-3, MXR Phase 90 as long-standing Grohl pedalboard constants; Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier and Vox AC30 confirmed live rig c. 2000)
Guitar Space — Everlong Amp Settings Guide (light-gain, clean-and-bright tone with grit appearing under hard picking)
Ground Guitar — Dave Grohl Guitars & Gear (Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier detail page)
tempo_note: 158 BPM, 4/4. Delay division chosen as 1/8 note (190ms at 158 BPM) for a tight rhythmic echo under the palm-muted intro/verse riff without smearing into slapback territory.

signal_chain.notes: S1 clean/verse: light-gain tone needs a fairly open gate to preserve pick dynamics and let the intended 'grit when picked hard' through. S2 chorus/heavy: RAT + pushed preamp needs a tighter gate to control the layered Drop D guitars.

signal_chain.based_on: Rig compensation (not a confirmed Everlong pedal)
signal_chain.notes: Standard Lace Sensor / Super Champ XD compensation — mild always-on saturation to simulate the amp-stage grit a hotter-output rig would have for free. Kept very low in the clean/verse snapshot so it only contributes the 'grit when you pick extra hard' character described in confirmed tone breakdowns, not audible gain. Raised ahead of the RAT in the chorus/heavy snapshot to push the front end harder.

CONFIRMED pedal — the driving, aggressive Everlong tone comes from a ProCo RAT into a cranked amp. Bypassed entirely in the clean/verse snapshot (intro/verse is light-gain, not RAT-driven). Active in the chorus/heavy snapshot as the primary gain source alongside the Cali Rectifire preamp push.
signal_chain.confirmed_source: Guitar.com / Reverb News: driving, aggressive Everlong tone from ProCo RAT distortion into a cranked amp

signal_chain.notes: EXPERIMENTAL preamp-only block (no cab/power-amp modeling), placed after Stupor OD/Ratatouille Dist and before Adriatic Delay per the preamp placement convention. S1 clean/verse: low Drive, amp-stage coloration only. S2 chorus/heavy: Drive and Master pushed further, Mid trimmed slightly for the scooped, aggressive Rectifier character, reinforcing the RAT rather than replacing it as the gain source.

signal_chain.based_on: BOSS DM-2 Analog Delay w/ Adrian Mod
signal_chain.notes: Confirmed long-standing constant on Grohl's pedalboard. Tempo-synced to 1/8 note (190ms at 158 BPM) for a tight rhythmic echo — more present under the clean/verse palm-muted riff, pulled back in the chorus/heavy snapshot so it doesn't wash out the layered Drop D guitars.

Compensates for the missing Dual Rectifier/Vox AC30 cab voicing and raises Level to help push the real tube amp's input stage. S1 clean/verse: gently brightened, minimal cut, keeping the light-gain tone clean and bright as described in confirmed tone breakdowns. S2 chorus/heavy: low end tightened and mids trimmed slightly to keep the layered Drop D guitars from getting muddy.

Room Size FIXED at 12m — a touch bigger and more modern than a tight studio room to suit the driving rock production, but still short/punchy overall rather than ambient. S1 clean/verse: slightly longer decay and higher mix for the more open intro/verse texture. S2 chorus/heavy: shorter decay, lower mix so the wall of layered guitars stays tight and driving.

signal_chain_notes: 7 of 8 available blocks used. Cali Rectifire (preamp-only, no cab/power-amp) placed after the overdrive/distortion blocks and before the delay block, per the AGENTS.md convention: pedals hit the amp's preamp stage first, modulation/time-based effects sit after the amp. Ratatouille Dist (RAT) is bypassed in the clean/verse snapshot and active in the chorus/heavy snapshot — the only toggled block; everything else stays on and just changes its parameters between snapshots.
preamp_experiment_note: EXPERIMENTAL Cali Rectifire block added because the Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier is specifically confirmed (not just era-plausible) as the amp the RAT was driving for Everlong's heavy tone. Kept at low/moderate Drive in the clean/verse snapshot so it only adds amp-stage warmth and touch response — the light-gain, almost-clean character there should come from Stupor OD alone, not this block. Pushed further in the chorus/heavy snapshot to reinforce the RAT's aggressive, driving character with real amp-stage push, while the RAT itself remains the primary gain source (consistent with the rig's usual pedals-do-the-gain, preamp-does-the-coloration approach).

1_clean_verse.description: Intro/verse tone. Ratatouille Dist bypassed — light-gain, clean-and-bright character with Stupor OD and Cali Rectifire kept low, just enough to let grit come through under hard picking, per confirmed Everlong tone breakdowns. Slightly more present tempo-synced delay (1/8 note) under the palm-muted riff. Represents: the palm-muted intro, verses, pre-choruses.

2_chorus_heavy.description: Chorus/bridge tone. Ratatouille Dist active, Cali Rectifire and Stupor OD pushed further for a driving, aggressive wall-of-guitar sound approximating the layered Drop D tracking on the record. Delay mix pulled back so it doesn't wash out the distortion. Represents: the full-band choruses and the bridge's heaviest moment.

playing_notes.tuning: Drop D throughout — confirmed for Everlong's layered guitar tracking.
playing_notes.quiet_loud_dynamic: Everlong's structure is a classic quiet/loud arrangement — intro and verses stay on Snapshot 1, choruses and the bridge's heaviest moment switch to Snapshot 2. Toggle on the downbeat where the full band and distorted guitar layer in.
playing_notes.picking_technique: Snapshot 1 is intentionally light-gain rather than fully clean — dig in on palm-muted notes to let the confirmed 'grit when you pick extra hard' character come through; don't expect a pristine clean tone.
playing_notes.preamp_caveat: The Cali Rectifire block is an experimental addition layered in front of the real Super Champ XD, not a replacement for it — if the heavy snapshot feels too saturated or compressed, try lowering Cali Rectifire Drive/Master before touching the RAT, since the RAT should remain the primary distortion character.
playing_notes.delay_note: Adriatic Delay is tempo-synced to 1/8 note (190ms at 158 BPM). Retap tempo if playing at a different reference BPM live.
